715	    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
716	    #
717	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
718	    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
719	    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
720	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.
721	
722	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
723	        node = self._parse_having_and()
724	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
725	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
726	        return node
727	
728	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
729	        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
730	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
731	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
732	        return node
733	
734	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
735	        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
736	        tok = self._peek()
737	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
738	            self._next()
739	            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
740	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
741	        return left
742	
743	    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
744	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
745	            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
746	        return self._parse_having_postfix()
747	
748	    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
749	        node = self._parse_having_operand()
750	        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
751	        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
752	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
753	            raise QueryValidationError(
754	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
755	            )
756	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
757	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
758	            self._expect_keyword("null")
759	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
760	        return node
761	
762	    def _parse_having_operand(self) -> tuple:
763	        tok = self._peek()
764	        if self._accept_op("("):
765	            node = self._parse_having_or()
766	            self._expect_op(")")
767	            return node
768	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
769	            # Only a signed numeric literal is accepted; unary +/- around a
770	            # column or aggregate is scalar arithmetic and stays rejected.
771	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
772	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
773	                self._next()
774	                self._next()
775	                value = nxt.value
776	                if isinstance(value, int):
777	                    if tok.value == "-":
778	                        value = -value
779	                    if not (_INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX):
780	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
781	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
782	                        )
783	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
784	                return ("literal", -value if tok.value == "-" else value, "float64")
785	            if nxt.kind == "eof":
786	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
787	                    f"expected a numeric literal after {tok.value!r} in HAVING"
788	                )
789	            raise QueryValidationError(
790	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
791	            )
792	        if tok.kind == "star":
793	            raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' is not allowed in HAVING")
794	        if tok.kind == "number":
795	            self._next()
796	            value = tok.value
797	            if isinstance(value, bool):
798	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
799	            return (
800	                "literal",
801	                value,
802	                "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64",
803	            )
804	        if tok.kind == "string":
805	            self._next()
806	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
807	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
808	            if (
809	                tok.kind == "ident"
810	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
811	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
812	                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
813	            ):
814	                func = tok.value.lower()
815	                self._next()  # function name
816	                self._expect_op("(")
817	                arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(
818	                    func
819	                )
820	                self._expect_op(")")
821	                return (
822	                    "hagg",
823	                    func.upper(),
824	                    arg,
825	                    arg_table,
826	                    arg_table_quoted,
827	                    distinct,
828	                )
829	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
830	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
831	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
832	            if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
833	                self._next()
834	                return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
835	            # An aggregate-style name not followed by '(' is a plain column.
836	            self._next()
837	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
838	        if tok.kind == "keyword":
839	            if tok.value == "case":
840	                raise QueryValidationError("CASE expressions are not allowed in HAVING")
841	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
842	                f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in HAVING expression"
843	            )
844	        raise QuerySyntaxError(
845	            f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in HAVING expression"
846	        )
847	
848	    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
849	
850	    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
851	        node = self._parse_and()
852	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
853	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
854	        return node
855	
856	    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
857	        node = self._parse_comparison()
858	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
859	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
860	        return node
861	
862	    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
863	        left = self._parse_not_factor()
864	        tok = self._peek()
865	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
866	            self._next()
867	            right = self._parse_not_factor()
868	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
869	        return left
870	
871	    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
872	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
873	            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
874	        return self._parse_postfix()
875	
876	    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
877	        node = self._parse_arith()
878	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
879	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
880	            self._expect_keyword("null")
881	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
882	        return node
883	
884	    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
885	    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.
886	
887	    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
888	        node = self._parse_term()
889	        while True:
890	            tok = self._peek()
891	            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
892	                self._next()
893	                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
894	            else:
895	                return node
896	
897	    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
898	        node = self._parse_factor()
899	        while True:
900	            tok = self._peek()
901	            if tok.kind == "star":
902	                self._next()
903	                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
904	            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
905	                self._next()
906	                node = ("arith", "/", node, self._parse_factor())
907	            else:
908	                return node
909	
910	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
911	        tok = self._peek()
912	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
913	            negate = tok.value == "-"
914	            self._next()
915	            nxt = self._peek()
916	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
917	                # A signed numeric literal is folded at parse time so the
918	                # signed int64 range check keeps its historical meaning
919	                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).
920	                self._next()
921	                value = nxt.value
922	                if isinstance(value, int):
923	                    if negate:
924	                        value = -value
925	                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
926	                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
927	                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
928	                        )
929	                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
930	                if negate:
931	                    value = -value
932	                return ("literal", value, "float64")

"""Pure SQL parsing: tokeniser, parsed statement tree and the parser.

This stage turns SQL text into a :class:`_Select` tree of plain tuples and
frozen data classes.  It is deliberately free of any file, schema, source
or join knowledge -- importing it never opens a file, and a
:class:`~columnar_analytics.errors.QuerySyntaxError` raised here always
surfaces before any source is read.  Later stages
(:mod:`columnar_analytics.resolve` for name resolution,
:mod:`columnar_analytics.binder` for schema binding) consume the parsed
tree; nothing here imports them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

from .errors import QuerySyntaxError, QueryValidationError


_KEYWORDS = frozenset(
    (
        "select",
        "distinct",
        "from",
        "where",
        "as",
        "not",
        "and",
        "or",
        "is",
        "null",
        "true",
        "false",
        "order",
        "by",
        "asc",
        "desc",
        "nulls",
        "first",
        "last",
        "limit",
        "group",
        "having",
        "inner",
        "left",
        "join",
        "on",
        "case",
        "when",
        "then",
        "else",
        "end",
    )
)

# Aggregate function names are ordinary (case-insensitive) identifiers that
# gain call syntax only in the projection and ORDER BY.
_AGG_NAMES = frozenset(("count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max"))
_INT64_MIN = -(2**63)
_INT64_MAX = 2**63 - 1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tokeniser
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Token:
    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
    value: Any
    text: str


_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
    r"""
    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
    """,
    re.VERBOSE,
)
# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)


def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
    if not isinstance(sql, str):
        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
    tokens: list[_Token] = []
    i = 0
    n = len(sql)
    while i < n:
        ch = sql[i]
        if ch.isspace():
            i += 1
            continue
        if ch == "*":
            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
            i += 1
            continue
        if ch in ",()+-/":
            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
            i += 1
            continue
        if ch in "=<>!":
            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
                i += 2
                continue
            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
                op = ch + "="
                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
                i += 2
                continue
            if ch in "=<>":
                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
                i += 1
                continue
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
        if ch == "'":
            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
            i = new_i
            continue
        if ch == '"':
            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
            i = new_i
            continue
        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
            if match:
                text = match.group(0)
                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
                i = match.end()
                continue
            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
            # used by multi-table queries ("table.column").
            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
            i += 1
            continue
        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
        if match:
            text = match.group(0)
            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
            i = match.end()
            continue
        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
    return tokens


def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
    lowered = word.lower()
    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
        if lowered == "true":
            return _Token("number", True, word)
        if lowered == "false":
            return _Token("number", False, word)
        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)


def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    parts: list[str] = []
    i = start + 1
    n = len(sql)
    while True:
        j = sql.find("'", i)
        if j == -1:
            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
        parts.append(sql[i:j])
        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
            parts.append("'")
            i = j + 2
            continue
        value = "".join(parts)
        try:
            value.encode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeEncodeError:
            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
        return value, j + 1


def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
    parts: list[str] = []
    i = start + 1
    n = len(sql)
    while True:
        j = sql.find('"', i)
        if j == -1:
            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
        parts.append(sql[i:j])
        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
            parts.append('"')
            i = j + 2
            continue
        value = "".join(parts)
        if not value:
            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
        return value, j + 1


def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
    try:
        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
            value: int | float = float(text)
        else:
            value = int(text, 10)
    except ValueError:
        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
    if isinstance(value, int):
        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
        return value
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
    return value
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parsed expression tree
#
# The parser emits plain tuples; qualifiers are resolved textually by the
# rewrite pass before binding.  Node tuples (pre-binding shape):
#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)
#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- + - * /
#   ("unary", operand, negate)
#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)
#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
#   ("not", operand)
#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
# The HAVING grammar additionally produces its own aggregate leaf:
#   ("hagg", func_upper, arg_name|"" , arg_table|None, arg_table_quoted, distinct)
# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary"/"case" nodes are value nodes.
#
# Binding turns those tuples into the single bound expression IR defined
# below (the :class:`_Expr` hierarchy).  Every later stage -- type and
# nullability derivation, dependency collection, plan rendering, predicate
# pushdown, the row-wise and the batched evaluator -- walks one bound node
# through the node's own declared fields, so a single bound expression is
# the consistent source of truth in single-table and join queries alike.
#
# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _RefItem:
    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""

    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
    distinct: bool = False  # kind == "agg": DISTINCT before the argument
    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
    descending: bool = False
    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
    # Table qualifiers (multi-table queries only; None when unqualified):
    table: str | None = None
    table_quoted: bool = False
    arg_table: str | None = None
    arg_table_quoted: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Join:
    """One equi-join step of a multi-table query.

    A statement may chain several steps in FROM/JOIN order; each step takes
    the intermediate result built so far as its left input and one freshly
    introduced table as its right input.
    """

    kind: str  # "inner" | "left" | "right" | "full"
    table: str  # right table name as spelled
    table_quoted: bool
    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)


@dataclass
class _Select:
    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
    table: str
    table_quoted: bool
    where: tuple | None
    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
    having: tuple | None
    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
    limit: int | None
    # Join steps in FROM/JOIN order; empty for a single-table statement.
    joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
    # SELECT DISTINCT: deduplicate the projected rows (non-aggregate only).
    distinct: bool = False

    @property
    def star(self) -> bool:
        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"

    @property
    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)

    @property
    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None


class _Parser:
    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))

    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.pos = 0
        # Multi-table statements (qualified names + join clauses) are only
        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
        # them as syntax errors.
        self._allow_join = allow_join

    def parse(self) -> _Select:
        select = self._parse_select()
        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
            tok = self._peek()
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
        return select

    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
        self._expect_keyword("select")
        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
        self._expect_keyword("from")
        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
        joins: tuple[_Join, ...] = ()
        if self._allow_join:
            joins = tuple(self._parse_join_clauses())
        where = None
        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
            where = self._parse_or()
        group_by = None
        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
            self._expect_keyword("by")
            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
            while self._accept_op(","):
                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
            group_by = tuple(names)
        having = None
        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
            having = self._parse_having_or()
        order_by = None
        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
            self._expect_keyword("by")
            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
            while self._accept_op(","):
                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
            order_by = tuple(order_items)
        limit = None
        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
            limit = self._parse_limit()
        return _Select(
            items=items,
            table=table_tok.value,
            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
            where=where,
            group_by=group_by,
            having=having,
            order_by=order_by,
            limit=limit,
            joins=joins,
            distinct=distinct,
        )

    def _parse_join_clauses(self) -> list[_Join]:
        # Zero or more join clauses may follow FROM; each introduces exactly
        # one new table with a single equi-ON condition.  "right" / "full" /
        # "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away from this clause (they are
        # matched with _accept_word), so columns carrying those names keep
        # working outside join parsing.
        joins: list[_Join] = []
        while True:
            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
                self._expect_keyword("join")
                joins.append(self._parse_join("inner"))
            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
                self._expect_keyword("join")
                joins.append(self._parse_join("left"))
            elif self._accept_word("right"):
                self._expect_keyword("join")
                joins.append(self._parse_join("right"))
            elif self._accept_word("full"):
                # Only the explicit FULL OUTER JOIN spelling is accepted.
                self._expect_word("outer")
                self._expect_keyword("join")
                joins.append(self._parse_join("full"))
            else:
                return joins

    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
        self._expect_keyword("on")
        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
        self._expect_op("=")
        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
        return _Join(
            kind=kind,
            table=table_tok.value,
            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
            left_key=left_key,
            right_key=right_key,
        )

    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
            )
        self._next()
        if not self._accept_op("."):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
            )
        nxt = self._peek()
        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
            )
        self._next()
        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)

    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
        while self._accept_op(","):
            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
        ):
            grouped_ahead = any(
                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
            )
            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
                raise QueryValidationError(
                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
                )
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
        return items

    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "star":
            self._next()
            return _RefItem("star")
        if (
            tok.kind == "ident"
            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
        ):
            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
            if self._arith_op_ahead():
                raise QueryValidationError(
                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
                )
            return item
        node = self._parse_arith()
        if node[0] == "column":
            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
            return _RefItem(
                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
            )
        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
        self._expect_keyword("as")
        alias = self._peek()
        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
            )
        self._next()
        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)

    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
        tok = self._peek()
        return tok.kind == "star" or (
            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
        )

    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
        descending = False
        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
            descending = False
        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
            descending = True
        nulls_first: bool | None = None
        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
                nulls_first = True
            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
                nulls_first = False
            else:
                tok = self._peek()
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
                )
        return _RefItem(
            item.kind,
            name=item.name,
            func=item.func,
            arg=item.arg,
            distinct=item.distinct,
            descending=descending,
            nulls_first=nulls_first,
            table=item.table,
            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
            arg_table=item.arg_table,
            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
        )

    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."

    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
        table_tok = self._next()
        self._expect_op(".")
        name_tok = self._peek()
        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
            )
        self._next()
        return _RefItem(
            "column",
            name=name_tok.value,
            table=table_tok.value,
            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
        )

    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
            return self._parse_qualified_column()
        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
        # can only be a plain column reference.
        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
            self._next()
            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
        func = tok.value.lower()
        self._next()  # consume the function name
        if not self._accept_op("("):
            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
        self._expect_op(")")
        return _RefItem(
            "agg",
            func=func.upper(),
            arg=arg,
            distinct=distinct,
            arg_table=arg_table,
            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
        )

    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
        # table-qualified) identifier, optionally preceded by DISTINCT.
        # Returns (name, table, table_quoted, distinct); name "" stands
        # for '*'.  DISTINCT only deduplicates the argument values of this
        # call; it accepts a single column reference only, and any other
        # use (a star, a missing argument, an expression, extra arguments
        # or a nested call) is a syntax error raised before any file is
        # opened.
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
            raise QueryValidationError(
                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
            )
        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "distinct":
            self._next()
            tok = self._peek()
            if tok.kind == "star":
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) does not accept '*'"
                )
            if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) requires one column argument, "
                    f"got {tok.text!r}"
                )
            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
                name, table, table_quoted = item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted
            else:
                self._next()
                name, table, table_quoted = tok.value, None, False
            nxt = self._peek()
            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column name, "
                    "not a function call"
                )
            if self._arith_op_ahead():
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"{func.upper()}(DISTINCT ...) argument must be a column "
                    "reference, not an expression"
                )
            return (name, table, table_quoted, True)
        if tok.kind == "star":
            if func != "count":
                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
            self._next()
            return ("", None, False, False)
        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
            )
        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
            nxt = self._peek()
            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
                )
            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted, False)
        self._next()
        nxt = self._peek()
        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
                raise QueryValidationError(
                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
                )
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
            )
        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
        return (tok.value, None, False, False)

    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
        if self._arith_op_ahead():
            raise QueryValidationError(
                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
            )

    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
        tok = self._peek()
        if (
            tok.kind != "number"
            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
        ):
            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
        self._next()
        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
            )
        return tok.value

    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
            return self._next()
        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")

    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
            raise QueryValidationError(
                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
            )
        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
        else:
            self._next()
            result = (None, False, tok.value)
        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
        if self._arith_op_ahead():
            raise QueryValidationError(
                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
            )
        return result

    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
    #
    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.

    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_having_and()
        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
        return node

    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
        return node

    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
            self._next()
            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
        return left

    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
        return self._parse_having_postfix()

    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_having_operand()
        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
        if self._arith_op_ahead():
            raise QueryValidationError(
                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
            )
        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
            self._expect_keyword("null")
            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
        return node

    def _parse_having_operand(self) -> tuple:
        tok = self._peek()
        if self._accept_op("("):
            node = self._parse_having_or()
            self._expect_op(")")
            return node
        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
            # Only a signed numeric literal is accepted; unary +/- around a
            # column or aggregate is scalar arithmetic and stays rejected.
            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
                self._next()
                self._next()
                value = nxt.value
                if isinstance(value, int):
                    if tok.value == "-":
                        value = -value
                    if not (_INT64_MIN <= value <= _INT64_MAX):
                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
                        )
                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
                return ("literal", -value if tok.value == "-" else value, "float64")
            if nxt.kind == "eof":
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    f"expected a numeric literal after {tok.value!r} in HAVING"
                )
            raise QueryValidationError(
                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
            )
        if tok.kind == "star":
            raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' is not allowed in HAVING")
        if tok.kind == "number":
            self._next()
            value = tok.value
            if isinstance(value, bool):
                return ("literal", value, "bool")
            return (
                "literal",
                value,
                "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64",
            )
        if tok.kind == "string":
            self._next()
            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
            if (
                tok.kind == "ident"
                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
                and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
            ):
                func = tok.value.lower()
                self._next()  # function name
                self._expect_op("(")
                arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted, distinct = self._parse_aggregate_args(
                    func
                )
                self._expect_op(")")
                return (
                    "hagg",
                    func.upper(),
                    arg,
                    arg_table,
                    arg_table_quoted,
                    distinct,
                )
            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
            if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
                self._next()
                return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
            # An aggregate-style name not followed by '(' is a plain column.
            self._next()
            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
        if tok.kind == "keyword":
            if tok.value == "case":
                raise QueryValidationError("CASE expressions are not allowed in HAVING")
            raise QuerySyntaxError(
                f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in HAVING expression"
            )
        raise QuerySyntaxError(
            f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in HAVING expression"
        )

    # WHERE expression grammar ------------------------------------------------

    def _parse_or(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_and()
        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
            node = ("or", node, self._parse_and())
        return node

    def _parse_and(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_comparison()
        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
            node = ("and", node, self._parse_comparison())
        return node

    def _parse_comparison(self) -> tuple:
        left = self._parse_not_factor()
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
            self._next()
            right = self._parse_not_factor()
            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
        return left

    def _parse_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
            return ("not", self._parse_not_factor())
        return self._parse_postfix()

    def _parse_postfix(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_arith()
        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
            self._expect_keyword("null")
            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
        return node

    # Arithmetic expressions (numeric scalar operands) ------------------------
    # Precedence (highest first): parentheses, unary +/-, * /, + -.

    def _parse_arith(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_term()
        while True:
            tok = self._peek()
            if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
                self._next()
                node = ("arith", tok.value, node, self._parse_term())
            else:
                return node

    def _parse_term(self) -> tuple:
        node = self._parse_factor()
        while True:
            tok = self._peek()
            if tok.kind == "star":
                self._next()
                node = ("arith", "*", node, self._parse_factor())
            elif tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "/":
                self._next()
                node = ("arith", "/", node, self._parse_factor())
            else:
                return node

    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
            negate = tok.value == "-"
            self._next()
            nxt = self._peek()
            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
                # A signed numeric literal is folded at parse time so the
                # signed int64 range check keeps its historical meaning
                # (-9223372036854775808 is valid, the bare magnitude is not).
                self._next()
                value = nxt.value
                if isinstance(value, int):
                    if negate:
                        value = -value
                    if not (-(2**63) <= value <= 2**63 - 1):
                        raise QuerySyntaxError(
                            "integer literal is outside the int64 range"
                        )
                    return ("literal", value, "int64")
                if negate:
                    value = -value
                return ("literal", value, "float64")
            if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident") and not (
                nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "("
            ) and not (nxt.kind == "keyword" and nxt.value == "case"):
                raise QuerySyntaxError(
                    "sign must be followed by a numeric literal or expression"
                )
            return ("unary", self._parse_factor(), negate)
        node = self._parse_atom()
        if (
            node[0] == "literal"
            and isinstance(node[1], int)
            and not isinstance(node[1], bool)
            and node[1] > 2**63 - 1
        ):
            # The magnitude 2**63 is only reachable through an explicit
            # negation; a bare literal must fit the signed int64 range.
            raise QuerySyntaxError("integer literal is outside the int64 range")
        return node

    def _parse_atom(self) -> tuple:
        if self._accept_op("("):
            node = self._parse_or()
            self._expect_op(")")
            return node
        if self._accept_keyword("case"):
            return self._parse_case()
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "number":
            self._next()
            value = tok.value
            if isinstance(value, bool):
                return ("literal", value, "bool")
            type_name = "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64"
            return ("literal", value, type_name)
        if tok.kind == "string":
            self._next()
            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
            if (
                tok.kind == "ident"
                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
                and nxt.kind == "op"
                and nxt.value == "("
            ):
                raise QueryValidationError(
                    f"aggregate {tok.value.upper()}(...) is not allowed here"
                )
            self._next()
            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
        if tok.kind == "keyword":
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected keyword {tok.text.upper()!r} in expression")
        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected token {tok.text!r} in expression")

    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form
        # (CASE value WHEN ...) is not supported.
        branches: list[tuple] = []
        while True:
            self._expect_keyword("when")
            condition = self._parse_or()
            self._expect_keyword("then")
            result = self._parse_arith()
            branches.append((condition, result))
            tok = self._peek()
            if not (tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "when"):
                break
        else_node = None
        if self._accept_keyword("else"):
            else_node = self._parse_arith()
        self._expect_keyword("end")
        return ("case", tuple(branches), else_node)

    # Token helpers -----------------------------------------------------------

    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
        return self.tokens[self.pos]

    def _next(self) -> _Token:
        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
        self.pos += 1
        return tok

    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
        if self._peek().kind == kind:
            self.pos += 1
            return True
        return False

    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
            self.pos += 1
            return True
        return False

    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
            self.pos += 1
            return True
        return False

    def _accept_word(self, value: str) -> bool:
        # Match a reserved word that is otherwise lexed as an ordinary
        # (non-keyword) identifier; used for RIGHT / FULL / OUTER, which keep
        # their meaning as column names outside the join clause.
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() == value:
            self.pos += 1
            return True
        return False

    def _expect_word(self, value: str) -> _Token:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind != "ident" or tok.value.lower() != value:
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
        return self._next()

    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")
        return self._next()

    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
        tok = self._peek()
        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")
        return self._next()

7	the binder, predicate pushdown, the executor and the explain plan -- walks
8	this single IR through the nodes' own declared fields, so semantics cannot
9	drift between stages.  The module depends only on the error types, the
10	parsed-literal constants and the format layer; it never sees files,
11	sources or join steps.
12	"""

23	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
24	# Bound expression IR -- one node hierarchy for every later stage
25	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
26	#
27	# Binding resolves a parsed tuple tree against one :class:`Schema` and
28	# produces :class:`_Expr` nodes.  Each node carries, once and for all:
29	#
30	# * ``type``     -- its static result type (``int64`` / ``float64`` /
31	#                   ``bool`` / ``utf8``); predicates are ``bool``;
32	# * ``nullable`` -- whether the node may yield NULL, derived while binding
33	#                   from the participating columns and the node kind;
34	# * ``columns()``-- every bound source-column index referenced anywhere in
35	#                   the subtree (multiplicity and in-tree order preserved);
36	# * ``children`` -- the node's direct bound subexpressions in fixed order,
37	#                   so generic traversals never re-switch on a node tag;
38	# * ``to_json()``-- its explain-plan condition / projection tree.
39	#
40	# Single-table statements and join chains bind against the same kind of
41	# (combined) :class:`Schema`, then share these exact nodes, rules and
42	# evaluators; adding an expression node later means adding one class here
43	# rather than teaching several parallel tuple-shape branches about it.
44	
45	
46	class _Expr:
47	    """One bound scalar value or boolean condition."""
48	
49	    __slots__ = ("type", "nullable", "children")
50	
51	    # Value node (literal / column / aggregate / unary / arith / case);
52	    # boolean predicates set this to False.
53	    is_value: bool = True
54	    # Accepted as a HAVING comparison / IS NULL operand (leaf references).
55	    is_having_leaf: bool = False

57	    def __init__(self, type_name: str, nullable: bool, children: tuple = ()):
58	        self.type = type_name
59	        self.nullable = nullable
60	        self.children = children

62	    def columns(self) -> list:
63	        """Bound source-column indices referenced in this subtree, in order."""
64	        indices: list = []
65	        for child in self.children:

77	        """Evaluate on one index batch; defaults to the row-wise semantics."""
78	        return [
79	            self.eval(_row_values(source_columns, i), agg_values) for i in batch

246	class _Case(_Expr):
247	    """A searched CASE: ordered (condition, result) branches and an ELSE."""
248	
249	    __slots__ = ("branches", "else_node")
250	
251	    def __init__(self, branches: tuple, else_node: _Expr | None, type_name: str):
252	        children = tuple(
253	            child for condition, result in branches for child in (condition, result)
254	        )
255	        if else_node is not None:
256	            children += (else_node,)
257	        nullable = else_node is None or any(
258	            result.nullable for _condition, result in branches
259	        ) or (else_node is not None and else_node.nullable)
260	        super().__init__(type_name, nullable, children)
261	        self.branches = branches
262	        self.else_node = else_node
263	
264	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
265	        # Written order is preserved; an omitted ELSE is rendered as null,
266	        # which also marks the implicit result nullable in the output schema.
267	        return {
268	            "kind": "case",
269	            "cases": [
270	                {"when": condition.to_json(), "then": result.to_json()}
271	                for condition, result in self.branches
272	            ],
273	            "else": None if self.else_node is None else self.else_node.to_json(),
274	        }
275	
276	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
277	        # Conditions are tried in written order; only TRUE matches.  FALSE
278	        # and UNKNOWN fall through, so unhit results are never evaluated:
279	        # their division-by-zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64
280	        # cannot raise.  The chosen result alone is evaluated.
281	        for condition, result in self.branches:
282	            if condition.eval(row, agg_values) is True:
283	                value = result.eval(row, agg_values)
284	                break
285	        else:
286	            value = (
287	                None
288	                if self.else_node is None
289	                else self.else_node.eval(row, agg_values)
290	            )
291	        if value is None:
292	            return None
293	        if self.type == "float64" and isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(
294	            value, bool
295	        ):
296	            return float(value)
297	        return value
298	
299	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
300	        # Each result expression is evaluated only on the sub-batch of rows
301	        # routed to it, so an error inside an unhit branch never raises;
302	        # rows no branch claimed fall through to ELSE (or NULL).
303	        result: list = [None] * len(batch)
304	        remaining = list(range(len(batch)))
305	        for condition, result_node in self.branches:
306	            if not remaining:
307	                break
308	            cond_values = condition.eval_batch(
309	                source_columns, [batch[k] for k in remaining], agg_values
310	            )
311	            taken = [k for k, cond in zip(remaining, cond_values) if cond is True]
312	            remaining = [
313	                k for k, cond in zip(remaining, cond_values) if cond is not True
314	            ]
315	            if taken:
316	                values = result_node.eval_batch(
317	                    source_columns, [batch[k] for k in taken], agg_values
318	                )
319	                for k, value in zip(taken, values):
320	                    result[k] = value
321	        if remaining and self.else_node is not None:
322	            values = self.else_node.eval_batch(
323	                source_columns, [batch[k] for k in remaining], agg_values
324	            )
325	            for k, value in zip(remaining, values):
326	                result[k] = value
327	        if self.type == "float64":
328	            # int64/float64 results unify to float64; ints become floats.
329	            return [self._unify_float(value) for value in result]
330	        return result
331	
332	    @staticmethod
333	    def _unify_float(value):
334	        if value is None:
335	            return None
336	        # int64/float64 results unify to float64; ints become floats.
337	        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
338	            return float(value)
339	        return value

440	class _Logic(_Predicate):
441	    """AND / OR; UNKNOWN propagates through either side."""
442	
443	    __slots__ = ("op", "left", "right")
444	
445	    def __init__(self, op: str, left: _Expr, right: _Expr):
446	        super().__init__(left.nullable or right.nullable, (left, right))
447	        self.op = op
448	        self.left = left
449	        self.right = right
450	
451	    def to_json(self) -> dict:
452	        return {
453	            "kind": "logic",
454	            "operator": self.op.upper(),
455	            "operands": [self.left.to_json(), self.right.to_json()],
456	        }
457	
458	    def eval(self, row: tuple, agg_values: tuple | None):
459	        # Short-circuit SQL semantics; UNKNOWN propagates only when needed.
460	        left = self.left.eval(row, agg_values)
461	        if self.op == "and":
462	            if left is False:
463	                return False
464	            right = self.right.eval(row, agg_values)
465	            if right is False:
466	                return False
467	            if left is None or right is None:
468	                return None
469	            return True
470	        if left is True:
471	            return True
472	        right = self.right.eval(row, agg_values)
473	        if right is True:
474	            return True
475	        if left is None or right is None:
476	            return None
477	        return False
478	
479	    def eval_batch(self, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None) -> list:
480	        left = self.left.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
481	        # Rows the left operand already decided (FALSE for AND, TRUE for
482	        # OR) never evaluate the right operand, exactly as row-wise
483	        # short-circuiting; the rest form the sub-batch evaluated next.
484	        if self.op == "and":
485	            undecided = [k for k, value in enumerate(left) if value is not False]
486	        else:
487	            undecided = [k for k, value in enumerate(left) if value is not True]
488	        result = list(left)
489	        if undecided:
490	            right = self.right.eval_batch(
491	                source_columns,
492	                [batch[k] for k in undecided],
493	                agg_values,
494	            )
495	            for k, rval in zip(undecided, right):
496	                lval = left[k]
497	                if self.op == "and":
498	                    result[k] = (
499	                        False
500	                        if rval is False
501	                        else (None if lval is None or rval is None else True)
502	                    )
503	                else:
504	                    result[k] = (
505	                        True
506	                        if rval is True
507	                        else (None if lval is None or rval is None else False)
508	                    )
509	        return result

512	def _bind_expr(node: tuple, schema: Schema) -> _Expr:
513	    tag = node[0]
514	    if tag == "literal":
515	        return _Literal(node[1], node[2])
516	    if tag == "column":
517	        name = node[1]
518	        try:
519	            index = schema.index(name)
520	        except KeyError:
521	            raise QueryValidationError(f"unknown column: {name!r}") from None
522	        col = schema.columns[index]
523	        return _Column(name, index, col.type, col.nullable)
524	    if tag == "not":
525	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
526	        _require_boolean(operand, "NOT")
527	        return _Not(operand)
528	    if tag in ("and", "or"):
529	        left = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
530	        right = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
531	        _require_boolean(left, tag.upper())
532	        _require_boolean(right, tag.upper())
533	        return _Logic(tag, left, right)
534	    if tag == "isnull":
535	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
536	        if not operand.is_value:
537	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
538	                "IS NULL operand must be a column reference or a literal"
539	            )
540	        return _IsNull(operand, node[2])
541	    if tag == "unary":
542	        operand = _bind_expr(node[1], schema)
543	        type_name = operand.type
544	        if type_name not in ("int64", "float64"):
545	            raise QueryValidationError(
546	                f"unary +/- requires a numeric operand, got {type_name}"
547	            )
548	        return _Unary(operand, node[2])
549	    if tag == "arith":
550	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
551	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
552	        left_t = left.type
553	        right_t = right.type
554	        if left_t not in ("int64", "float64") or right_t not in ("int64", "float64"):
555	            raise QueryValidationError(
556	                f"arithmetic requires numeric operands, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
557	            )
558	        op = node[1]
559	        out_type = (
560	            "float64"
561	            if op == "/" or "float64" in (left_t, right_t)
562	            else "int64"
563	        )
564	        return _Arith(op, left, right, out_type)
565	    if tag == "case":
566	        bound_branches = []
567	        result_types: list[str] = []
568	        for cond_node, result_node in node[1]:
569	            cond = _bind_expr(cond_node, schema)
570	            _require_boolean(cond, "WHEN")
571	            result = _bind_expr(result_node, schema)
572	            bound_branches.append((cond, result))
573	            result_types.append(result.type)
574	        else_bound = None
575	        if node[2] is not None:
576	            else_bound = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
577	            result_types.append(else_bound.type)
578	        out_type = _unify_case_types(result_types)
579	        return _Case(tuple(bound_branches), else_bound, out_type)
580	    if tag == "cmp":
581	        op = node[1]
582	        left = _bind_expr(node[2], schema)
583	        right = _bind_expr(node[3], schema)
584	        if not (left.is_value and right.is_value):
585	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
586	                "comparison operands must be column references or literals"
587	            )
588	        _check_comparison_types(op, left, right)
589	        return _Cmp(op, left, right)
590	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive
591

593	def _check_comparison_types(op: str, left: _Expr, right: _Expr) -> None:
594	    """Validate the static operand types of one comparison (WHERE and HAVING)."""
595	    left_t = left.type
596	    right_t = right.type
597	    if "bool" in (left_t, right_t):
598	        if left_t != "bool" or right_t != "bool":
599	            raise QueryValidationError(
600	                f"bool can only be compared to bool, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
601	            )
602	        if op not in ("=", "!="):
603	            raise QueryValidationError(f"bool only supports = and !=, not {op!r}")
604	    elif "utf8" in (left_t, right_t):
605	        if left_t != "utf8" or right_t != "utf8":
606	            raise QueryValidationError(
607	                f"utf8 can only be compared to utf8, got {left_t} and {right_t}"
608	            )
609	    elif not {left_t, right_t} <= {"int64", "float64"}:
610	        raise QueryValidationError(
611	            f"cannot compare values of type {left_t} and {right_t}"
612	        )

615	def _unify_case_types(types: list[str]) -> str:
616	    """Unify the static types of every reachable CASE result.
617	
618	    int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64; bool and utf8 must
619	    match every other result exactly.  Anything else is incompatible.
620	    """
621	    unique = set(types)
622	    if unique <= {"int64", "float64"}:
623	        return "float64" if "float64" in unique else "int64"
624	    if len(unique) == 1:
625	        return next(iter(unique))
626	    raise QueryValidationError(
627	        "CASE results must have consistent types: "
628	        + ", ".join(sorted(unique))
629	    )

639	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
640	# Three-valued-logic evaluation
641	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
642	#
643	# The per-row semantics live on the bound expression nodes themselves
644	# (:meth:`_Expr.eval`); a batch failure falls back to that same row-at-a-
645	# time method (see :func:`_eval_batch`) so the reported first error keeps
646	# its historical row order.  The batched semantics
647	# (:meth:`_Expr.eval_batch`) visit exactly the same
648	# (row, subexpression) pairs.
649	
650	
651	def _compare_values(op: str, left, right) -> bool:
652	    """The boolean result of one comparison on two non-NULL values."""
653	    if op == "=":
654	        result = left == right
655	    elif op == "!=":
656	        result = left != right
657	    elif op == "<":
658	        result = left < right
659	    elif op == "<=":
660	        result = left <= right
661	    elif op == ">":
662	        result = left > right
663	    else:  # ">="
664	        result = left >= right
665	    return bool(result)
666	
667	
668	def _negate_value(value):
669	    # Unary minus: the type is preserved; only int64 can overflow.
670	    if isinstance(value, int):
671	        if value == _INT64_MIN:
672	            raise QueryValidationError(
673	                "negating the int64 minimum overflows the int64 range"
674	            )
675	        return -value
676	    return -value
677	
678	
679	def _arith_value(op: str, left, right):
680	    # int64 op int64 stays int64 for + - *; any float64 operand or a
681	    # division produces float64.  NULLs are handled by the caller.
682	    if op == "/" or isinstance(left, float) or isinstance(right, float):
683	        if op == "/" and right == 0:
684	            raise QueryValidationError("division by zero")
685	        a = float(left)
686	        b = float(right)
687	        if op == "+":
688	            result = a + b
689	        elif op == "-":
690	            result = a - b
691	        elif op == "*":
692	            result = a * b
693	        else:
694	            result = a / b
695	        if not math.isfinite(result):
696	            raise QueryValidationError(
697	                "float64 arithmetic produced a non-finite value"
698	            )
699	        return result
700	    if op == "+":
701	        result = left + right
702	    elif op == "-":
703	        result = left - right
704	    else:
705	        result = left * right
706	    if not (_INT64_MIN <= result <= _INT64_MAX):
707	        raise QueryValidationError("int64 arithmetic overflowed the int64 range")
708	    return result
709

711	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
712	# Batched column-vector evaluation
713	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
714	#
715	# The row-processing stages -- the WHERE filter, the ORDER BY sort keys,
716	# the SELECT expressions and the projection feeding SELECT DISTINCT -- share
717	# one batched evaluator.  Each stage hands the next a set of valid row
718	# indices; an expression is evaluated one *batch* of rows at a time against
719	# the source columns and yields one vector of result values aligned with
720	# the batch, instead of re-entering the row-at-a-time control flow for
721	# every row.  The vectorised walk is the node's own ``eval_batch``; its
722	# semantics are exactly those of :meth:`_Expr.eval` (NULL propagation,
723	# three-valued logic, per-row CASE short-circuit, the int64 / float64
724	# error rules).  Because the batched walk visits the same
725	# (row, subexpression) pairs as the row-wise walk, any batch that contains
726	# a failing row raises; the driver then re-runs that batch row by row so
727	# the reported error is byte-identical to the historical one.
728	
729	_EVAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2048
730	
731	
732	def _iter_batches(indices, size=_EVAL_BATCH_SIZE):
733	    """Yield ``indices`` sliced into consecutive batches of at most ``size``."""
734	    for start in range(0, len(indices), size):
735	        yield indices[start : start + size]
736	
737	
738	def _eval_batch(node: _Expr, source_columns, batch, agg_values: tuple | None = None) -> list:
739	    """Evaluate one batch of a bound expression, returning a value vector.
740	
741	    ``batch`` is the current valid-row set (row indices into
742	    ``source_columns``); the returned list holds one value per batch row, in
743	    batch order.  A :class:`QueryValidationError` anywhere in the batch is
744	    re-raised through the row-wise reference path so the exact historical
745	    error (and its row order) surfaces.
746	    """
747	    try:
748	        return node.eval_batch(source_columns, batch, agg_values)
749	    except QueryValidationError:
750	        # The batched walk visits the same (row, subexpression) pairs as
751	        # the row-wise one, so this re-run raises the same first error the
752	        # pre-vectorised engine reported for these rows.
753	        return [node.eval(_row_values(source_columns, i), agg_values) for i in batch]
754

756	def _eval_expr_selection(node, source_columns, selected) -> list:
757	    """Evaluate ``node`` over the row indices ``selected``, batch by batch.
758	
759	    Returns one list of values aligned with ``selected``; shared by the
760	    WHERE filter, the ORDER BY sort keys and the SELECT projections.
761	    """
762	    values: list = []
763	    for batch in _iter_batches(selected):
764	        values.extend(_eval_batch(node, source_columns, batch))
765	    return values
766	
767	
768	def _filter_rows(where: _Expr, source_columns, row_count: int) -> list[int]:
769	    """The row indices whose WHERE condition evaluates to TRUE.
770	
771	    Batched counterpart of the historical row loop: rows are evaluated
772	    batch by batch in file order, and FALSE and UNKNOWN both drop the row.
773	    """
774	    selected: list[int] = []
775	    for batch in _iter_batches(list(range(row_count))):
776	        mask = _eval_batch(where, source_columns, batch)
777	        selected.extend(i for i, keep in zip(batch, mask) if keep is True)
778	    return selected
779	def _row_values(source_columns: tuple[tuple, ...], i: int) -> tuple:
780	    return tuple(col[i] for col in source_columns)

1	"""Binding: resolve a parsed statement against one schema.
2	
3	The binder consumes the parsed :class:`~columnar_analytics.parser._Select`
4	tree and a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Schema` (single-file,
5	combined join or metadata-derived -- all the same kind) and produces the
6	bound plan dict: validated projection items, the bound WHERE / HAVING
7	expression IR, ORDER BY keys and the aggregate registry.  It performs no
8	file access of its own, so a statement can be bound against metadata alone
9	(the explain path) or against a fully read table (the execution path) with
10	identical results and identical
11	:class:`~columnar_analytics.errors.QueryValidationError` behaviour.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	from dataclasses import dataclass

20	    _Aggregate,
21	    _Case,
22	    _Column,
23	    _Cmp,
24	    _Expr,
25	    _IsNull,
26	    _Literal,
27	    _Logic,
28	    _Not,
29	    _bind_expr,

42	@dataclass(frozen=True)
43	class _BoundItem:
44	    """A validated projection element."""
45	
46	    kind: str  # "column" | "agg" | "expr"
47	    output_name: str
48	    # kind == "column":
49	    col_index: int = -1
50	    # kind == "agg":
51	    func: str = ""
52	    arg_index: int = -1  # -1 means COUNT(*)
53	    arg_type: str = ""
54	    distinct: bool = False  # argument values are deduplicated per group
55	    # kind == "expr":
56	    expr: tuple | None = None  # bound scalar expression
57	    out_type: str = ""

61	def _bind_select(select: _Select, schema: Schema, expected_table="input") -> dict:
62	    if expected_table is not None:
63	        table_matches = (
64	            select.table == expected_table
65	            if select.table_quoted
66	            else select.table.lower() == expected_table.lower()
67	        )
68	        if not table_matches:
69	            raise QueryValidationError(
70	                f"unknown table {select.table!r}; only {expected_table!r} is supported"
71	            )
72	
73	    where = _bind_expr(select.where, schema) if select.where is not None else None
74	    if where is not None and where.type != "bool":
75	        raise QueryValidationError(
76	            f"WHERE clause must be boolean, got {where.type}"
77	        )
78	
79	    if select.distinct and select.is_aggregate_query:
80	        raise QueryValidationError(
81	            "DISTINCT is not allowed with GROUP BY, HAVING or aggregate projections"
82	        )
83	
84	    if not select.is_aggregate_query:
85	        return _bind_plain(select, schema, where)
86	    return _bind_aggregate(select, schema, where)

89	def _bind_plain(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
90	    # Non-aggregate path: '*' or a comma-separated list of plain columns and
91	    # computed scalar expressions (each named with AS).
92	    bound_items: list[_BoundItem] = []
93	    if select.star:
94	        for i, col in enumerate(schema.columns):
95	            bound_items.append(
96	                _BoundItem(
97	                    "column",
98	                    output_name=col.name,
99	                    col_index=i,
100	                    out_type=col.type,
101	                    nullable=col.nullable,
102	                )
103	            )
104	    else:
105	        output_seen: set[str] = set()
106	        for item in select.items:
107	            if item.kind == "star":
108	                # A star mixed into a plain projection remains grammatical.
109	                raise QuerySyntaxError("'*' cannot be mixed with other projection items")
110	            if item.kind == "column":
111	                name = item.name
112	                if name in output_seen:
113	                    raise QueryValidationError(
114	                        f"duplicate column in projection: {name!r}"
115	                    )
116	                try:
117	                    col_index = schema.index(name)
118	                except KeyError:

120	                col = schema.columns[col_index]

122	                bound_items.append(
123	                    _BoundItem(

125	                        output_name=col.name,
126	                        col_index=col_index,

128	                        nullable=col.nullable,
129	                    )
130	                )

132	                expr = _bind_expr(item.expr, schema)

135	                # expression may additionally yield bool or utf8 results
136	                # (its own WHEN/ELSE type consistency is checked at binding).
137	                if isinstance(expr, _Case):
138	                    allowed_types = ("int64", "float64", "bool", "utf8")
139	                else:

142	                    raise QueryValidationError(
143	                        f"SELECT expression must be numeric, got {out_type}"
144	                    )
145	                alias = item.name
146	                if alias in output_seen:
147	                    raise QueryValidationError(f"duplicate result column: {alias!r}")
148	                output_seen.add(alias)

153	                        expr=expr,

156	                    )
157	                )

159	        item.output_name: item.expr for item in bound_items if item.kind == "expr"
160	    }
161	    projected = {item.output_name: i for i, item in enumerate(bound_items)}
162	    order_by = _bind_plain_order_by(
163	        select.order_by, schema, aliases, select.distinct, projected
164	    )
165	    return {
166	        "mode": "plain",
167	        "items": tuple(bound_items),
168	        "aggregates": (),
169	        "where": where,
170	        "having": None,
171	        "order_by": order_by,
172	        "distinct": select.distinct,
173	    }

176	def _bind_plain_order_by(
177	    select_order_by, schema: Schema, aliases: dict, distinct: bool, projected: dict
178	):
179	    if select_order_by is None:
180	        return None
181	    bound: list[tuple] = []
182	    order_seen: set[str] = set()
183	    for item in select_order_by:
184	        if item.kind == "agg":
185	            raise QueryValidationError(
186	                f"aggregate {item.func}({_arg_label(item)}) may appear in ORDER BY "
187	                "only as part of an aggregate query"
188	            )
189	        name = item.name
190	        if name in order_seen:
191	            raise QueryValidationError(
192	                f"duplicate column in ORDER BY: {name!r}"
193	            )
194	        order_seen.add(name)
195	        nulls_first = item.nulls_first if item.nulls_first is not None else False
196	        if distinct:

198	            # ORDER BY name must be one of the projected outputs (a bare

205	                        f"unknown ORDER BY column: {name!r}"
206	                    ) from None

209	                )

213	        if name in aliases:

216	        try:

226	def _bind_aggregate(select: _Select, schema: Schema, where) -> dict:
227	    if select.star:
228	        raise QueryValidationError("'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY")
229	
230	    if (

281	                    distinct=distinct,

291	    output_seen: set[str] = set()
292	    has_plain = False
293	    for item in select.items:
294	        if item.kind == "star":
295	            raise QueryValidationError(
296	                "'*' cannot be combined with aggregates or GROUP BY"
297	            )
298	        if item.kind == "expr":
299	            raise QueryValidationError(
300	                "scalar expressions are not supported in aggregate queries"
301	            )
302	        if item.kind == "column":
303	            has_plain = True
304	            name = item.name
305	            try:
306	                col_index = schema.index(name)
307	            except KeyError:

309	            if col_index not in group_index_set:
310	                raise QueryValidationError(
311	                    f"column {name!r} must appear in GROUP BY or be wrapped in an aggregate"
312	                )
313	            label = name
